title: He should have died that night.
paragraphs: He should have died that night.

One decision.
One strike.
One perfectly timed attack—and David’s story would have ended in the dark.
That was the plan.

Ahithophel, the brilliant strategist, gave Absalom a blueprint so sharp it almost feels terrifying to read: “Let me choose twelve thousand men… we will attack David while he is weary and weak… I will strike down only the king” (2 Samuel 17:1–2, paraphrased).

Clean.
Efficient.
Devastating.

No wasted movement.
No drawn-out war.
Just one surgical blow—and the throne would be secured.
And here’s what should shake you:
It was good counsel.
Even the Bible implies it.
If Absalom had listened, David would likely have fallen.
Pause there.
Because some of you are facing situations right now where the enemy’s strategy looks just like that—tight, logical, almost unstoppable.

The betrayal is calculated.
The opposition is organized.
The timing is brutal.
And you can feel it—
“This might be the end.”
But then…
Hushai speaks.

Not louder.
Not stronger.
But wiser.
He steps into the tension and paints a different picture:
“David is not weak. He is a warrior. A man of war. Cornered. Dangerous. Like a bear robbed of her cubs” (2 Samuel 17:8, paraphrased).
Then he does something subtle—almost surgical.
He feeds Absalom’s pride.
“Don’t rush this. Gather all Israel. From Dan to Beersheba. Let YOU lead them.”
That’s the pivot.

Not strategy.
Ego.
And Absalom chooses Hushai’s counsel over Ahithophel’s.
Why?
Scripture pulls back the curtain:
“For the LORD had ordained to defeat the good counsel of Ahithophel, so that the LORD might bring harm upon Absalom.” (2 Samuel 17:14)
Don’t miss that.
God didn’t just respond.
He ordained.
He didn’t merely react to events—He ruled over them.
Even the “best” plan against David was already marked for collapse.
Let this sink into your bones:
The enemy can have a good plan… and still lose.
Because your life is not ultimately in the hands of strategy, intelligence, or timing.
It is in the hands of a sovereign God.
And when He decides to protect, preserve, or redirect—
no human brilliance can override Him.
Listen, kapatid…
Some of you are losing sleep over plans formed in rooms you’re not even in.

Conversations you can’t control.
Decisions made without you.
Attacks you didn’t see coming.
You’re trying to outthink what’s coming.
But God is already ahead of it.

He can flip a decision.
Delay an attack.
Confuse the counsel.
Expose the hidden.
Or simply cause the “perfect” plan to fall apart.
Not by accident.
By design.
But the story doesn’t stop with David.
Because David is not the final King.
There is another.

Another anointed One.
Another rejected King.
Another man surrounded by betrayal and calculated schemes.
Jesus.
When He stood before His enemies, the plans against Him didn’t fail.
They succeeded.

Judas betrayed Him with precision.
Religious leaders plotted with intent.
Rome executed with power.
No Hushai stepped in to stop it.
No alternative counsel interrupted the cross.
Why?
Because this time, the “plan” was not being overturned.
It was being fulfilled.
Acts 2:23 says Jesus was delivered up “according to the definite plan and foreknowledge of God.”
Let that hit you.
The greatest evil ever committed—the قتل of the sinless Son of God—was not outside God’s control.
It was the very means of your salvation.
Where David was spared by disrupted counsel…
Jesus was sacrificed by fulfilled counsel.
Why?
So that rebels like us—traitors at heart, aligned more with Absalom than David—could be forgiven.
That’s the Gospel.
Not that God always stops the attack…
but that He uses even the worst attack to accomplish the greatest redemption.
So when you look at your life and see chaos, opposition, or even collapse—
don’t rush to conclude that God has lost control.
He may be doing something deeper.
Something eternal.
Something that doesn’t just save your situation…
but saves your soul.
Here’s the call:

Repent.
Return.
Trust the true King.

Because one day, every false throne will fall.
Every proud Absalom will be brought low.
Every hidden counsel will be exposed.
And only the Kingdom of Christ will stand.
So don’t anchor your hope in what you can control.
Anchor it in the God who controls what you can’t.
Because from scandal to grace—
Jesus rewrites everything.
Someone out there is one decision away from despair—and one truth away from hope.
